# Ordinary types from two examples

This bounded study addresses [#22 criterion 10](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/issues/22).
Two separate author agents received only their stored two-example prompts,
with no forked conversation history, tools, repository reads, execution or
repairs. Each returned four first programs and predictions. The observer
supplied schema-2/edition-2026 Qargo transport metadata afterward. This is the
declared local authoring protocol, not authenticated external authorship or a
controlled model benchmark. The exact deployment/sampling settings are unavailable.

The first [context](context.md) contains the observer's incorrect
`std::transform::init0` example. Its four original sources and all twelve actual
finite/selected check/run observations are preserved. Every call rejects that
imported name at bytes 97–102 (`project` in finite, `name` in selected). None
reaches the intended type or owner condition. These refusals do not count as
successful negative type/ownership controls, nor do the attempted runs execute
their intended programs.

The second [context](context-02.md) corrects only the example API namespace to
`std::quantum::init0`. A new author received that prompt without the first
response or diagnostics and independently wrote four new first programs. This
is registered consecutively as `attempt-02`; it is not a source repair by the
informed observer. Both attempts retain their own context, predictions and
pre-check file inventory. No implementation or API was changed to fit either prompt.

| Corrected first program | Actual finite and selected results |
| --- | --- |
| `copy-ordinary` | Both checks and runs pass. A helper ignores its second ordinary Bit and duplicates its first; run returns `(0,0)` with probability 1. |
| `observe-pair` | Both checks and runs pass. Each quantum input is explicitly observed once; run returns `(0,0)` with probability 1. |
| `implicit-readout` | Both checks reject bytes 130–137: expected `Bit`, found `Q<Bit>` (`type_mismatch` in finite, `type` in selected). |
| `duplicate-owner` | Both checks reject the second use of `q` at bytes 212–213 with `ownership`. |

The corrected twelve observations comprise four successful checks, four
successful runs and four intended semantic refusals. They agree with that
author's stored predictions. Both source collections use ordinary Bit/products
and explicit `Q<Bit>` without inventing `CBit`, `CBits` or `C<>`; only the
corrected context reaches the intended type/ownership controls. The prompt
itself specifies the requested positive and deliberately invalid tasks, so
this is bounded evidence of using two examples, not an unrestricted discovery
or general model-capability claim. All-zero closed outputs cannot distinguish
a swapped pair order or prove arbitrary-state/reference behavior.

Both captures use the same fixed CLI,
`/private/tmp/qleisli-classical-functions-after`, SHA-256
`8291ddad7119af45ec24fe6c1a9266384470b4d0556ebedd6c0c87b710844e5a`,
and native file SHA-256
`39effde0f152a2c926fcea3a7f99fc2f25f9de65906be2b8c527508353c90c85`.
Every observation retains actual argument lists, timestamp, exit, raw stream
hashes and identities before/after its call. These local hashes do not
authenticate build provenance, child-start identity or compiler correctness.

See the [first inventory](first-files.json), [first predictions](predictions.json),
[first capture](observations/capture.json), [second inventory](first-files-02.json),
[second predictions](predictions-02.json), [second capture](observations-02/capture.json),
[assessment](assessment.json) and [session](session.json). Registration checks
these records without replaying historical commands. Selected positive results
disclose `native-validity`, `source_steps_checked: true` and
`source_meaning_verified: false`.

These 24 observations do not establish full CI success, Issue completion,
generic source preservation, a resource theorem or a new guarantee. The
broader QS/PR/quantitative RS/EXACT duties and the two ordinary decoded-QLV1
ownership/scope guarantees retain their existing status and scope. No generic
QFT or maximum-size experiment is included.
